evidence.claim: Highway 27 winds 43 miles north from Highway 20 to Prineville on the Lower Crooked River Back Country Byway.
evidence.quote: Highway 27 winds 43 miles north from Highway 20 to the city of Prineville.

evidence.claim: The southern 18 miles are graded gravel suitable for passenger vehicles, crossing a landscape of private ranches, public rangeland, rolling hills and basalt buttes.
evidence.quote: the southernmost 18 miles are unpaved but are of high-standard graded gravel suitable for a passenger vehicle. Private ranches are interspersed among public rangelands with views of rolling hills and towering basaltic buttes.

evidence.claim: BLM’s byway description pairs that open country with the gorge of the Crooked Wild and Scenic River, where campgrounds, day-use areas and a hiking trail line the river.
evidence.quote: Nine year-round campgrounds, two day-use areas and a hiking trail line the wild and scenic river stretch of this byway.

evidence.claim: The entire route remains a state highway.

evidence.claim: The river corridor changed in 1961 when the Bureau of Reclamation built Bowman Dam.
evidence.quote: The dam was constructed by the United States Bureau of Reclamation in 1961

evidence.claim: Its reservoir flooded a canyon of juniper and sagebrush as part of the Crooked River Project. Irrigation storage was the primary purpose, with flood control and recreation secondary.
evidence.quote: The reservoir is part of the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation's Crooked River Project, flooding a juniper- and sagebrush-filled canyon, and was finished in 1961.

evidence.claim: Irrigation storage was the primary purpose, with flood control and recreation secondary.
evidence.quote: is primarily an irrigation storage water body, with secondary objectives of Crooked River flood control and public recreation.

evidence.claim: The dam took the name of Arthur Ray Bowman, a Prineville businessman who had supported the project.
evidence.quote: Because of his dedication to the project, the dam was renamed the Arthur R. Bowman Dam in his honor.

evidence.claim: Arthur Ray Bowman, a Prineville businessman
evidence.quote: The museum is named after Arthur Ray Bowman, a Prineville businessman and civic leader.

evidence.claim: Behind the dam, Prineville Reservoir extends along 18 miles of the Crooked River, storing water upstream of the drive through the gorge.
evidence.quote: Prineville Reservoir covers 18 miles (29 km) of the Crooked River and is primarily an irrigation storage water body

evidence.claim: Driving north, reach pavement before crossing Bowman Dam’s spillway and descending into the Chimney Rock river segment.
evidence.quote: After the paved section begins, the back country byway crosses the spillway of Bowman Dam before descending into the gorge of the Chimney Rock segment of the Crooked Wild and Scenic River

evidence.claim: The drive finishes in Prineville, where the Bowman Museum occupies the old Crook County Bank building.
evidence.quote: The A. R. Bowman Memorial Museum is a local history museum in Prineville, Oregon, United States.  Opened in 1971, the museum is housed in the old Crook County Bank Building

evidence.claim: Bronze teller cages and marble counters remain inside the Bowman Museum, which occupies Prineville’s former Crook County Bank.
evidence.quote: The first floor still has the bank's original bronze teller cages, marble counter tops

evidence.claim: The two-story building was constructed in 1910 with stone from a local quarry west of the Ochoco Viewpoint.
evidence.quote: The building was constructed in 1910.  It is a two-story Romanesque style building constructed using stone blocks from a local quarry located west of the Ochoco Viewpoint.

evidence.claim: Arthur Bowman bought the building for his title and insurance business after Prineville National Bank became insolvent during the Great Depression.
evidence.quote: When that bank became insolvent during the Great Depression, the building was purchased by A. R. Bowman for his title and insurance business.

evidence.claim: His wife and two daughters donated it to Crook County in 1971 for use as a museum.
evidence.quote: In 1971, Bowman's wife and two daughters donated the Crook County Bank building to Crook County for use as a museum.

evidence.claim: The banking rooms now hold exhibits on the local railroad and timber industry, with historic photographs, furniture and tools alongside the original teller fittings.
evidence.quote: This includes exhibits on the City of Prineville Railroad, the local timber industry and United States Forest Service as well as pioneer furniture, garments, tools, and other artifacts.
